thread:
amira: quick idea dump 1: what if instead of swapping tokens immediately we do a timed 'holdback' on demotes for N seconds and use a smoothing window to pick demote candidates? would reduce thrash during spikes.

sam: short answer: sounds promising. long answer: need to ensure we don't violate read-after-write and we keep fairness. how do you pick N?

amira: propose adaptive N: base_holdback = 5s; multiplier = min(1 + incoming_rate/1000, 8). so during surges holdback grows. we still signal owner to prepare but don't allow eviction to proceed until holdback expires unless forced.

ravi: i like avoiding immediate token transfer. but if holdback just delays the inevitable, could we starve low-traffic tenants when many big tenants spike?

amira: safety: we run a soft-quota per-tenant that guarantees a minimum residency fraction. if many prefixes are pending demote but below tenant minimum, we promote them in selection. basically two-tier selection: protected prefixes (by quota) and candidates.

tess: can you show selection pseudo?

amira: ```
selectDemoteCandidates(shard, metrics) -> list[prefix] {
  window := metrics.access_window_seconds // e.g., 60s
  score(p) := (p.accesses/window) / max(1, p.kv_tokens/200)
  // apply holdback if recently signalled
  if now - p.demote_signalled_at < p.holdback_seconds { score(p) = score(p) * 0.01 }
  // enforced tenant quota boost
  if tenantIsBelowQuota(p.tenant) { score(p) *= 1.5 }
  return topk(score, k=shard.eviction_slots)
}
```

sam: interesting. so holdback makes candidates temporarily unlikely. how do we implement the signalling? durable marker in prefix metadata?

amira: yes. demote_signalled_at is written to prefix metadata (idempotent). owners subscribe to prefix notifications via stream; on signal owner can opt-in to prefetch/kickprefill or reply 'lock' if they need more time.

ravi: how do operators observe this? need clear metrics or we'll be blind.

amira: add these metrics: prefix.holdback.seconds_p50/p95, prefix.demote.signals_per_min, tenant.protected_fraction, shard.eviction.slots_filled. also event log for demote_signalled and demote_forced.

tess: rollout plan? ops-bot wants small changes.

amira: rollout:
- sim with 24h production trace (no writes)
- enable signal-only mode in prod for 12h (emits metrics)
- enable active holdback on canary 3 nodes for 48h serving low-risk tenants
- ramp by region with monitoring gates

sam: failure modes? what if owners ignore signals and we end up with many stale holdbacks?

amira: add TTL for holdback marker (max_holdback=30m) and background reconciler that clears stale marks if owner heartbeat missing. forced demote API available to ops.

ravi: testing checklist: unit tests for multiplier math, integration for signal stream + owner opt-in, chaos test that stubs owners not responding.

tess: small UX note: expose per-tenant "min_residency_pct" config so product can tune for paying customers.

ops-bot: canary ticket created: https://internal.redwood/ops/canaries/holdback-smoothing-2026 (draft) :eyes:

amira: runbook stub (paste):
```
Runbook: holdback-smoothing incident steps
1) Flip cluster feature flag: holdback=false
2) Check metrics: shard.eviction.slots_filled and prefix.holdback.seconds_p95
3) If handoff.latency_p99 > baseline*1.8 -> disable holdback on region and force demote for top affected prefixes
4) If many stale markers detected (>1000 in 10m) -> run reconciler: POST $ADMIN/prefixes/reconcile?threshold=600
5) Collect: prefix metadata dump, owner-heartbeat logs, demote_signalled event stream
```

sam: please include RFC link when you open. also add a small dashboard tile showing protected vs candidate counts.

amira: will do. opening RFC follow-up: https://go.redwood/rfc/holdback-smoothing (WIP) :rocket:

ravi: LGTM. small ask: document invariants clearly at top of RFC (read-after-write, no token release without owner ack).

amira: will add. thanks all.
